non_blocking_finding.status: FIXED during the follow-up review pass (see review_pass_2 below) -- kept here for the review-history record
non_blocking_finding.summary: detectAllergens' exact-token matching does not strip trailing punctuation (e.g. a trailing '*'), but EU-labeled products commonly mark exactly these 26 allergens with a trailing asterisk/footnote marker directly in the printed ingredient list -- the real-world implementation of Annex III's declaration requirement. Text captured verbatim that way (e.g. 'Limonene*') will not match the seed's 'Limonene' under current exact Set-equality, so the badge could silently fail to appear on a meaningful share of real labels.
non_blocking_finding.why_not_blocking: Neither the source brief nor the spec's acceptance criteria mention the asterisk convention, so no written AC is failed and no existing test catches it -- this is a gap the design itself has, not a deviation from it. The feature is already release-gated on separate regulatory content sign-off.
non_blocking_finding.recommended_fix: Strip a trailing run of non-alphanumeric marks (*, †, footnote digits) in allergenDetector.ts's normalizeToken before comparison; add allergenDetector.test.ts cases for asterisk-suffixed real-label-style input.
non_blocking_finding.recommended_timing: Before the release-gate sign-off lands, not before this code review closes.

review_pass_2.trigger: user-requested 'review' after the ACCEPT verdict above
review_pass_2.outcome: Upgraded the non_blocking_finding above from suspected to CONFIRMED by direct execution: the asterisk case is a COMPLETE failure (zero matches, not partial), and a second related pattern was found and confirmed -- parenthetical fragrance-breakdown groups (e.g. 'Parfum (Linalool, Limonene, Citronellol)') lose their first and last entries to punctuation merging.
review_pass_2.fix_applied: src/utils/allergenDetector.ts normalizeToken now strips leading/trailing non-alphanumeric decoration. Fully fixes the asterisk case and the last entry of a parenthetical group. Does NOT fix the first entry of a parenthetical group (internal '(' merges with the preceding label word) -- fixing that would require treating '(' as a new token delimiter, which would break seed entries whose own canonical name legitimately contains parentheses. Documented as a known remaining limitation in the function's doc comment and locked in by an explicit test, not left silent.
review_pass_2.tests_added: 4 new cases in allergenDetector.test.ts's 'tolerates common real-label decoration' suite -- asterisk-suffix fix, parenthetical last-entry fix, parenthetical first-entry known-limitation lock, and an internal-parentheses regression guard.
